articleTitle: Erratum to: Sums of Linear Transformations in Higher Dimensions
ON THE MORITA REDUCED VERSIONS OF SKEW GROUP ALGEBRAS OF PATH ALGEBRAS
abstract: Let <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$R$</tex> be the skew group algebra of a finite group acting on the path algebra of a quiver. This article develops both theoretical and practical methods to do computations in the Morita-reduced algebra associated to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$R$</tex>. Reiten and Riedtmann proved that there exists an idempotent <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$e$</tex> of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$R$</tex> such that the algebra <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$eRe$</tex> is both Morita equivalent to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$R$</tex> and isomorphic to the path algebra of some quiver, which was described by Demonet. This article gives explicit formulas for the decomposition of any element of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$eRe$</tex> as a linear combination of paths in the quiver described by Demonet. This is done by expressing appropriate compositions and pairings in a suitable monoidal category, which takes into account the representation theory of the finite group.

articleTitle: Genericity and Universality for Operator Ideals
abstract: A bounded linear operator <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$U$</tex> between Banach spaces is universal for the complement of some operator ideal <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathfrak{J}$</tex> if it is a member of the complement and it factors through every element of the complement of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathfrak{J}$</tex>. In the first part of this paper, we produce new universal operators for the complements of several ideals, and give examples of ideals whose complements do not admit such operators. In the second part of the paper, we use descriptive set theory to study operator ideals. After restricting attention to operators between separable Banach spaces, we call an operator ideal <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathfrak{J}$</tex> generic if whenever an operator <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$A$</tex> has the property that every operator in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathfrak{J}$</tex> factors through a restriction of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$A$</tex>, then every operator between separable Banach spaces factors through a restriction of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$A$</tex>. We prove that many classical operator ideals (such as strictly singular, weakly compact, Banach–Saks) are generic and give a sufficient condition, based on the complexity of the ideal, for when the complement does not admit a universal operator. Another result is a new proof of a theorem of M. Girardi and W. B. Johnson, which states that there is no universal operator for the complement of the ideal of completely continuous operators.

articleTitle: A SPECIAL CASE OF QUASIMINIMALITY FOR THE COMPLEX EXPONENTIAL FIELD
abstract: We obtain a non-trivial special case of Zilber's quasiminimality conjecture for the complex exponential field. Specifically, we deal with those subsets of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbb{C}$</tex> defined by formulas of the form <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\exists \bar{y}(P(x,\bar{y})=0)$</tex>, where <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$P$</tex> is a term formed from the language <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\{+,\times ,\exp \}$</tex> together with parameters from <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbb{C}$</tex>.

articleTitle: A BESSEL DELTA METHOD AND EXPONENTIAL SUMS FOR GL(2)
abstract: In this paper, we introduce a simple Bessel <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\delta $</tex>-method to the theory of exponential sums for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\textrm{GL}_2$</tex>. Some results of Jutila on exponential sums are generalized in a less technical manner to holomorphic newforms of arbitrary level and nebentypus. In particular, this gives a short proof for the Weyl-type subconvex bound in the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$t$</tex>-aspect for the associated <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$L$</tex>-functions.

articleTitle: Deformations Of Multivalued Harmonic Functions
abstract: We consider harmonic sections of a bundle over the complement of a codimension 2 submanifold in a Riemannian manifold, which can be thought of as multivalued harmonic functions. We prove a result to the effect that these are stable under small deformations of the data. The proof is an application of a version of the Nash-Moser implicit function theorem.

articleTitle: Sequential Regular Variation: Extensions of Kendall's Theorem
abstract: Regular variation is a continuous-parameter theory; we work in a general setting, containing the existing Karamata, Bojanic–Karamata/de Haan and Beurling theories as special cases. We give sequential versions of the main theorems, that is, with sequential rather than continuous limits. This extends the main result, a theorem of Kendall's (which builds on earlier work of Kingman and Croft), to the general setting.

articleTitle: On Katz's (A,B)-Exponential Sums
abstract: We deduce Katz's theorems for (A, B)-exponential sums over finite fields using <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\ell$</tex>-adic cohomology and a theorem of Denef–Loeser, removing the hypothesis that A + B is relatively prime to the characteristic p. In some degenerate cases, the Betti number estimate is improved using toric decomposition and Adolphson–Sperber's bounds for degrees of L-functions. Applying the facial decomposition theorem, we prove that the universal family of (A, B)-polynomials is generically ordinary for its L-function when p is in certain arithmetic progression.

articleTitle: Moduli Spaces of Generalized Hyperpolygons
abstract: We introduce the notion of generalized hyperpolygon, which arises as a representation, in the sense of Nakajima, of a comet-shaped quiver. We identify these representations with rigid geometric figures, namely pairs of polygons: one in the Lie algebra of a compact group and the other in its complexification. To such data, we associate an explicit meromorphic Higgs bundle on a genus-g Riemann surface, where g is the number of loops in the comet, thereby embedding the Nakajima quiver variety into a Hitchin system on a punctured genus-g Riemann surface (generally with positive codimension). We show that, under certain assumptions on flag types, the space of generalized hyperpolygons admits the structure of a completely integrable Hamiltonian system of Gelfand–Tsetlin type, inherited from the reduction of partial flag varieties. In the case where all flags are complete, we present the Hamiltonians explicitly. We also remark upon the discretization of the Hitchin equations given by hyperpolygons, the construction of triple branes (in the sense of Kapustin–Witten mirror symmetry), and dualities between tame and wild Hitchin systems (in the sense of Painlevé transcendents).

articleTitle: The central sphere of an ALE space
abstract: We consider the induced metric on the spherical fixed point set of a circle action on an ALE space and describe it by using the algebraic geometry of rational curves on algebraic surfaces, in particular the lines on a cubic.

articleTitle: On Squares of Sums of Three Cubes
abstract: We show that almost every positive integer can be expressed as a sum of four squares of integers represented as the sums of three positive cubes.

articleTitle: On Bourgain's Counterexample for the Schrödinger Maximal Function
abstract: This paper provides a rigorous derivation of a counterexample of Bourgain, related to a well-known question of pointwise a.e. convergence for the solution of the linear Schrödinger equation, for initial data in a Sobolev space. This counterexample combines ideas from analysis and number theory, and the present paper demonstrates how to build such counterexamples from first principles, and then optimize them.

articleTitle: Counting Algebraic Points in Expansions of O-Minimal Structures by a Dense Set
abstract: The Pila–Wilkie theorem states that if a set <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$X\subseteq \mathbb{R}^n$</tex> is definable in an o-minimal structure <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathcal{R}$</tex> and contains ‘many’ rational points, then it contains an infinite semialgebraic set. In this paper, we extend this theorem to an expansion <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\widetilde{\mathcal{R}}=\langle {\mathcal{R}}, P\rangle$</tex> of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\mathcal{R}}$</tex> by a dense set P, which is either an elementary substructure of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\mathcal{R}}$</tex>, or it is <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{dcl}$</tex>-independent, as follows. If X is definable in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\widetilde{\mathcal{R}}$</tex> and contains many rational points, then it is dense in an infinite semialgebraic set. Moreover, it contains an infinite set which is <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\emptyset}$</tex>-definable in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\langle \overline{\mathbb{R}}, P\rangle$</tex>, where <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\overline{\mathbb{R}}$</tex> is the real field. Along the way we introduce the notion of the ‘algebraic trace part’ <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$X^{{\, alg}}_t$</tex> of any set <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$X\subseteq \mathbb{R}^n$</tex>, and we show that if X is definable in an o-minimal structure, then <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$X^{{\, alg}}_t$</tex> coincides with the usual algebraic part of X.

articleTitle: Instantons and Bows for the Classical Groups
abstract: The construction of Atiyah, Drinfeld, Hitchin and Manin provided complete description of all instantons on Euclidean four-space. It was extended by Kronheimer and Nakajima to instantons on ALE spaces, resolutions of orbifolds <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbb{R}^4/\Gamma$</tex> by a finite subgroup Γ⊂SU(2). We consider a similar classification, in the holomorphic context, of instantons on some of the next spaces in the hierarchy, the ALF multi-Taub-NUT manifolds, showing how they tie in to the bow solutions to Nahm’s equations via the Nahm correspondence. Recently Nakajima and Takayama constructed the Coulomb branch of the moduli space of vacua of a quiver gauge theory, tying them to the same space of bow solutions. One can view our construction as describing the same manifold as the Higgs branch of the mirror gauge theory as described by Cherkis, O’Hara and Saemann. Our construction also yields the monad construction of holomorphic instanton bundles on the multi-Taub-NUT space for any classical compact Lie structure group.

articleTitle: Separating singular moduli and the primitive element problem
abstract: We prove that <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${|x-y|\ge 800X^{-4}}$</tex>, where <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$x$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$y$</tex> are distinct singular moduli of discriminants not exceeding <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$X$</tex>. We apply this result to the ‘primitive element problem’ for two singular moduli. In a previous article, Faye and Riffaut show that the number field <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${{\mathbb{Q}}}(x,y)$</tex>, generated by two distinct singular moduli <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$x$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$y$</tex>, is generated by <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${x-y}$</tex> and, with some exceptions, by <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${x+y}$</tex> as well. In this article we fix a rational number <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\alpha \ne 0,\pm 1}$</tex> and show that the field <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${{\mathbb{Q}}}(x,y)$</tex> is generated by <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${x+\alpha y}$</tex>, with a few exceptions occurring when <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$x$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$y$</tex> generate the same quadratic field over <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${{\mathbb{Q}}}$</tex>. Together with the above-mentioned result of Faye and Riffaut, this generalizes a theorem due to Allombert et al. (2015) about solutions of linear equations in singular moduli.

articleTitle: Galois Action on Homology of Generalized Fermat Curves
abstract: The fundamental group of Fermat and generalized Fermat curves is computed. These curves are Galois ramified covers of the projective line with abelian Galois groups H. We provide a unified study of the action of both cover Galois group H and the absolute Galois group <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{Gal}(\bar{\mathbb{Q}}/\mathbb{Q})$</tex> on the pro-<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\ell$</tex> homology of the curves in study. Also the relation to the pro-<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\ell$</tex> Burau representation is investigated.

articleTitle: Tilting Modules and Dominant Dimension with Respect to Injective Modules
abstract: In this paper, we study a relationship between tilting modules with finite projective dimension and dominant dimension with respect to injective modules as a generalization of results of Crawley-Boevey–Sauter, Nguyen–Reiten–Todorov–Zhu and Pressland–Sauter. Moreover, we give characterizations of almost n-Auslander–Gorenstein algebras and almost n-Auslander algebras by the existence of tilting modules. As an application, we describe a sufficient condition for almost 1-Auslander algebras to be strongly quasi-hereditary by comparing such tilting modules and characteristic tilting modules.

articleTitle: The Alternating Block Decomposition of Iterated Integrals and Cyclic Insertion on Multiple Zeta Values
abstract: The cyclic insertion conjecture of Borwein, Bradley, Broadhurst and Lisoněk states that by inserting all cyclic permutations of some initial blocks of 2's into the multiple zeta value ζ(1, 3, … , 1, 3) and summing, one obtains an explicit rational multiple of a power of π. Hoffman gives a conjectural identity of a similar flavour concerning <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$ 2 \zeta(3,3,\{2\}^m) - \zeta(3,\{2\}^m,1,2) $</tex>. In this paper, we introduce the ‘generalized cyclic insertion conjecture’, which we describe using a new combinatorial structure on iterated integrals—the so-called alternating block decomposition. We see that both the original BBBL cyclic insertion conjecture, and the Hoffman's conjectural identity, are special cases of this generalized cyclic insertion conjecture. By using Brown's motivic MZV framework, we establish that some symmetrized version of the generalized cyclic insertion conjecture always holds, up to a rational; this provides some evidence for the generalized conjecture.

articleTitle: Infinite-Parameter ADHM Transform
abstract: The Atiyah–Drinfeld–Hitchin–Manin transform and its various generalizations are examples of nonlinear integral transforms between finite-dimensional moduli spaces. This note describes a natural infinite-dimensional generalization, where the transform becomes a map from boundary data to a family of solutions of the self-duality equations in a domain.

articleTitle: The Index Theorem for Toeplitz Operators as a Corollary of Bott Periodicity
abstract: This is an expository paper about the index of Toeplitz operators, and in particular Boutet de Monvel’s theorem [5]. We prove Boutet de Monvel’s theorem as a corollary of Bott periodicity, and independently of the Atiyah-Singer index theorem.

articleTitle: Coherency and Constructions for Monoids
abstract: A monoid S is right coherent if every finitely generated subact of every finitely presented right S-act is finitely presented. This is a finiteness condition, and we investigate whether or not it is preserved under some standard algebraic and semigroup theoretic constructions: subsemigroups, homomorphic images, direct products, Rees matrix semigroups, including Brandt semigroups, and Bruck–Reilly extensions. We also investigate the relationship with the property of being weakly right noetherian, which requires all right ideals of S to be finitely generated.

articleTitle: Segal’s Gamma rings and universal arithmetic
abstract: Segal’s Γ-rings provide a natural framework for absolute algebraic geometry. We use G. Almkvist’s global Witt construction to explore the relation with J. Borger <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\mathbb F}_1$</tex>-geometry and compute the Witt functor-ring <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\mathbb W}_0({\mathbb S})$</tex> of the simplest Γ-ring <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\mathbb S}$</tex>. We prove that it is isomorphic to the Galois invariant part of the BC-system, and exhibit the close relation between λ-rings and the Arithmetic Site. Then, we concentrate on the Arakelov compactification <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\overline{{\rm Spec\,}{\mathbb Z}}}$</tex> which acquires a structure sheaf of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\mathbb S}$</tex>-algebras. After supplying a probabilistic interpretation of the classical theta invariant of a divisor D on <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\overline{{\rm Spec\,}{\mathbb Z}}}$</tex>, we show how to associate to D a Γ-space that encodes, in homotopical terms, the Riemann–Roch problem for D.

articleTitle: Volume of Line Bundles via Valuation Vectors (Different from Okounkov Bodies)
abstract: Up to a factor 1/n!, the volume of a big line bundle agrees with the Euclidean volume of its Okounkov body. The latter is the convex hull of top rank valuation vectors of sections, all with respect to a single flag. In this paper, we give a new volume formula, valid in the ample cone. It is also based on top rank valuation vectors, but mixes data coming from several different flags.

articleTitle: Characteristic Cohomology I: Singularities of Given Type
abstract: For a germ of a variety <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathcal{V}, 0 \subset \mathbb C^N, 0$</tex>, a singularity <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathcal{V}_0$</tex> of ‘type <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathcal{V}$</tex>’ is given by a germ <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$f_0 : \mathbb C^n, 0 \to \mathbb C^N, 0$</tex> which is transverse to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathcal{V}$</tex> in an appropriate sense so that <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathcal{V}_0 = f_0^{\,-1}(\mathcal{V})$</tex>. If <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathcal{V}$</tex> is a hypersurface germ, then so is <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathcal{V}_0 $</tex>, and by transversality <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\operatorname{codim}}_{\mathbb C} {\operatorname{sing}}(\mathcal{V}_0) = {\operatorname{codim}}_{\mathbb C} {\operatorname{sing}}(\mathcal{V})$</tex> provided <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$n \gt {\operatorname{codim}}_{\mathbb C} {\operatorname{sing}}(\mathcal{V})$</tex>. So <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathcal{V}_0, 0$</tex> will exhibit singularities of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathcal{V}$</tex> up to codimension n. For singularities <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathcal{V}_0, 0$</tex> of type <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathcal{V}$</tex>, we introduce a method to capture the contribution of the topology of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathcal{V}$</tex> to that of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathcal{V}_0$</tex>. It is via the ‘characteristic cohomology’ of the Milnor fiber (for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathcal{V}, 0$</tex> a hypersurface), and complement and link of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathcal{V}_0$</tex> (in the general case). The characteristic cohomology of the Milnor fiber <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathcal{A}_{\mathcal{V}}(\,f_0; R)$</tex>, and respectively of the complement <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathcal{C}_{\mathcal{V}}(\,f_0; R)$</tex>, are subalgebras of the cohomology of the Milnor fibers, respectively the complement, with coefficients R in the corresponding cohomology. For a fixed <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathcal{V}$</tex>, they are functorial over the category of singularities of type <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathcal{V}$</tex>. In addition, for the link of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathcal{V}_0$</tex> there is a characteristic cohomology subgroup <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathcal{B}_{\mathcal{V}}(\,f_0, \mathbf{k})$</tex> of the cohomology of the link over a field <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{k}$</tex> of characteristic 0. The cohomologies <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathcal{C}_{\mathcal{V}}(\,f_0; R)$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathcal{B}_{\mathcal{V}}(\,f_0, \mathbf{k})$</tex> are shown to be invariant under the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathcal{K}_{\mathcal{V}}$</tex>-equivalence of defining germs f<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf>, and likewise <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathcal{A}_{\mathcal{V}}(\,f_0; R)$</tex> is shown to be invariant under the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathcal{K}_{H}$</tex>-equivalence of f<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf> for H the defining equation of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathcal{V}, 0$</tex>. We give a geometric criterion involving ‘vanishing compact models’ for both the Milnor fibers and complements which detect non-vanishing subalgebras of the characteristic cohomologies, and subgroups of the characteristic cohomology of the link. Also, we consider how in the hypersurface case the cohomology of the Milnor fiber is a module over the characteristic cohomology <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathcal{A}_{\mathcal{V}}(\,f_0; R)$</tex>. We briefly consider the application of these results to a number of cases of singularities of a given type. In part II, we specialize to the case of matrix singularities and using results on the topology of the Milnor fibers, complements and links of the varieties of singular matrices obtained in another paper allow us to give precise results for the characteristic cohomology of all three types.

articleTitle: Morse Theory without Non-Degeneracy
abstract: We describe an extension of Morse theory to smooth functions on compact Riemannian manifolds, without any non-degeneracy assumptions except that the critical locus must have only finitely many connected components.

articleTitle: Consistency of M-Theory on Non-Orientable Manifolds
abstract: We prove that there is no parity anomaly in M-theory in the low-energy field theory approximation. Our approach is computational. We determine the generators for the 12-dimensional bordism group of pin manifolds with a w<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf>-twisted integer lift of w<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf>; these are the manifolds on which Wick-rotated M-theory exists. The anomaly cancellation comes down to computing a specific η-invariant and cubic form on these manifolds. Of interest beyond this specific problem are our expositions of computational techniques for η-invariants, the algebraic theory of cubic forms, Adams spectral sequence techniques and anomalies for spinor fields and Rarita–Schwinger fields.

articleTitle: Unit Equations on Quaternions
abstract: A classical result about unit equations says that if Γ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf> and Γ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> are finitely generated subgroups of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\mathbb C}^\times$</tex>, then the equation x + y = 1 has only finitely many solutions with x ∈ Γ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf> and y ∈ Γ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>. We study a non-commutative analogue of the result, where <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Gamma_1,\Gamma_2$</tex> are finitely generated subsemigroups of the multiplicative group of a quaternion algebra. We prove an analogous conclusion when both semigroups are generated by algebraic quaternions with norms greater than 1 and one of the semigroups is commutative. As an application in dynamics, we prove that if f and g are endomorphisms of a curve C of genus 1 over an algebraically closed field k, and deg( f), deg(g)≥ 2, then f and g have a common iterate if and only if some forward orbit of f on C(k) has infinite intersection with an orbit of g.

articleTitle: An Application of Wall-Crossing to Noether–Lefschetz Loci
abstract: Consider a smooth projective 3-fold <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$X$</tex> satisfying the Bogomolov–Gieseker conjecture of Bayer–Macrì–Toda (such as <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\mathbb{P}}^3$</tex>, the quintic 3-fold or an abelian 3-fold). Let <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$L$</tex> be a line bundle supported on a very positive surface in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$X$</tex>. If <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$c_1(L)$</tex> is a primitive cohomology class, then we show it has very negative square.

articleTitle: On Uniqueness of Dirichlet Series
abstract: We give a characterization of the ratio of two Dirichelt series convergent in a right half-plane under an analytic condition, which is applicable to a uniqueness problem for Dirichlet series admitting analytic continuation in the complex plane as meromorphic functions of finite order; uniqueness theorems are given in terms of a-points of the functions.

articleTitle: Volumes And Random Matrices
abstract: This article is an introduction to newly discovered relations between volumes of moduli spaces of Riemann surfaces or super Riemann surfaces, simple models of gravity or supergravity in two dimensions, and random matrix ensembles. (The article is based on a lecture at the conference on the Mathematics of Gauge Theory and String Theory, University of Auckland, January 2020)

articleTitle: Coherent Systems on the Projective Line
abstract: It is well known that there are no stable bundles of rank greater than 1 on the projective line. In this paper, our main purpose is to study the existence problem for stable coherent systems on the projective line when the number of sections is larger than the rank. We include a review of known results, mostly for a small number of sections.

articleTitle: Subconvexity Bounds for Twisted L-Functions
abstract: We prove hybrid subconvexity bounds for a wide class of twisted L-functions L(s, f × χ) at the central point, including a new instance of the Weyl subconvexity bound.

articleTitle: Skyrmions, Tetrahedra and Magic Numbers
abstract: Michael Atiyah’s interest in Skyrmions and their relationship to monopoles and instantons is recalled. Some approximate models of Skyrmions with large baryon numbers are then considered. Skyrmions having particularly strong binding are clusters of unit baryon number Skyrmions arranged as truncated tetrahedra. Their baryon numbers, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$B = 4 \,, 16 \,, 40 \,, 80 \,, 140 \,, 224$</tex>, are the tetrahedral numbers multiplied by four, agreeing with the magic proton and neutron numbers <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$2 \,, 8 \,, 20 \,, 40 \,, 70 \,, 112$</tex> occurring in the nuclear shell model in the absence of strong spin-orbit coupling.

articleTitle: THE AVERAGE NUMBER OF SUBGROUPS OF ELLIPTIC CURVES OVER FINITE FIELDS
abstract: By adapting the technique of David, Koukoulopoulos and Smith for computing sums of Euler products, and using their interpretation of results of Schoof à la Gekeler, we determine the average number of subgroups (or cyclic subgroups) of an elliptic curve over a fixed finite field of prime size. This is in line with previous works computing the average number of (cyclic) subgroups of finite abelian groups of rank at most <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$2$</tex>. A required input is a good estimate for the divisor function in both short interval and arithmetic progressions, that we obtain by combining ideas of Ivić–Zhai and Blomer. With the same tools, an asymptotic for the average of the number of divisors of the number of rational points could also be given.

articleTitle: POINCARÉ DUALITY, CAP PRODUCT AND BOREL–MOORE INTERSECTION HOMOLOGY
abstract: Using a cap product, we construct an explicit Poincaré duality isomorphism between the blown-up intersection cohomology and the Borel–Moore intersection homology, for any commutative ring of coefficients and second-countable, oriented pseudomanifolds.

articleTitle: ON A FORMULA FOR THE REGULARIZED DETERMINANT OF ZETA FUNCTIONS WITH APPLICATION TO SOME DIRICHLET SERIES
abstract: In this paper, we study a large class of zeta functions. We evaluate explicitly the special values of these zeta functions and the associated derivatives at <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$0$</tex>. As an application, we recover several results on the zeta functions defined by two polynomials already obtained in the literature.

articleTitle: DISTORTION OF SPHERES AND SURFACES IN SPACE
abstract: It is known that the surface of a cone over the unit disc with large height has smaller distortion than the standard embedding of the 2-sphere in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbb{R}^3$</tex>. In this note we show that distortion minimizers exist among convex embedded 2-spheres and have uniformly bounded eccentricity. Moreover, we prove that <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\pi /2$</tex> is a sharp lower bound on the distortion of embedded closed surfaces of positive genus.

articleTitle: SMOOTH, NONSYMPLECTIC EMBEDDINGS OF RATIONAL BALLS IN THE COMPLEX PROJECTIVE PLANE
abstract: We exhibit an infinite family of rational homology balls, which embed smoothly but not symplectically in the complex projective plane. We also obtain a new lattice embedding obstruction from Donaldson's diagonalization theorem and use this to show that no two of our examples may be embedded disjointly.

articleTitle: The Bruce–Roberts Number of A Function on A Hypersurface with Isolated Singularity
abstract: Let <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(X,0)$</tex> be an isolated hypersurface singularity defined by <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\phi \colon ({\mathbb{C}}^n,0)\to ({\mathbb{C}},0)$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$f\colon ({\mathbb{C}}^n,0)\to{\mathbb{C}}$</tex> such that the Bruce–Roberts number <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mu _{BR}(f,X)$</tex> is finite. We first prove that <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mu _{BR}(f,X)=\mu (f)+\mu (\phi ,f)+\mu (X,0)-\tau (X,0)$</tex>, where <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mu $</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\tau $</tex> are the Milnor and Tjurina numbers respectively of a function or an isolated complete intersection singularity. Second, we show that the logarithmic characteristic variety <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$LC(X,0)$</tex> is Cohen–Macaulay. Both theorems generalize the results of a previous paper by some of the authors, in which the hypersurface <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(X,0)$</tex> was assumed to be weighted homogeneous.

articleTitle: On the First Hochschild Cohomology of Cocommutative Hopf Algebras of Finite Representation Type
abstract: Let <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathscr{B}_0({\mathcal{G}})\subseteq k\,{\mathcal{G}}$</tex> be the principal block algebra of the group algebra <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$k\,{\mathcal{G}}$</tex> of an infinitesimal group scheme <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\mathcal{G}}$</tex> over an algebraically closed field <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$k$</tex> of characteristic <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\operatorname{char}}(k)=:p\geq 3$</tex>. We calculate the restricted Lie algebra structure of the first Hochschild cohomology <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\mathcal{L}}:={\operatorname{H}}^1(\mathscr{B}_0({\mathcal{G}}),\mathscr{B}_0({\mathcal{G}}))$</tex> whenever <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathscr{B}_0({\mathcal{G}})$</tex> has finite representation type. As a consequence, we prove that the complexity of the trivial <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\mathcal{G}}$</tex>-module <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$k$</tex> coincides with the maximal toral rank of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\mathcal{L}}$</tex>.

articleTitle: A NOTE ON RATIONAL HOMOLOGICAL STABILITY OF AUTOMORPHISMS OF MANIFOLDS
abstract: By work of Berglund and Madsen, the rings of rational characteristic classes of fibrations and smooth block bundles with fibre <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$D^{2n}\sharp (S^n\times S^n)^{\sharp g}$</tex>, relative to the boundary, are for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$2n\ge 6$</tex> independent of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$g$</tex> in degrees <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$*\le (g-6)/2$</tex>. In this note, we explain how this range can be improved to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$*\le g-2$</tex> using cohomological vanishing results due to Borel and the classical invariant theory. This implies that the analogous ring for smooth bundles is independent of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$g$</tex> in the same range, provided the degree is small compared to the dimension.

articleTitle: Rational Points on Elliptic K3 Surfaces of Quadratic Twist Type
abstract: In studying rational points on elliptic K3 surfaces of the form <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$$\begin{equation*} f(t)y^2=g(x), \end{equation*}$$</tex> where f, g are cubic or quartic polynomials (without repeated roots), we introduce a condition on the quadratic twists of two elliptic curves having simultaneously positive Mordell–Weil rank. We prove a necessary and sufficient condition for the Zariski density of rational points by using this condition, and we relate it to the Hilbert property. Applying to surfaces of Cassels–Schinzel type, we prove unconditionally that rational points are dense both in Zariski topology and in real topology.

articleTitle: Transverse hilbert schemes, bi-hamiltonian systems and hyperkähler geometry
abstract: We give a characterization of Atiyah’s and Hitchin’s transverse Hilbert schemes of points on a symplectic surface in terms of bi-Poisson structures. Furthermore, we describe the geometry of hyperkähler manifolds arising from the transverse Hilbert scheme construction, with particular attention paid to the monopole moduli spaces.

articleTitle: Continuity Points Via Riesz Potentials for ℂ-Elliptic Operators
abstract: We establish a Riesz potential criterion for Lebesgue continuity points of functions of bounded <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbb{A}$</tex>-variation, where <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbb{A}$</tex> is a <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbb{C}$</tex>-elliptic differential operator of arbitrary order. This result generalizes a potential criterion that is known for full gradients to the case where full gradient estimates are not available by virtue of Ornstein's non-inequality.

articleTitle: Cohomology of the Universal Smooth Cubic Surface
abstract: We compute the rational cohomology of the universal family of smooth cubic surfaces using Vassiliev's method of simplicial resolution. Modulo embedding, the universal family has cohomology isomorphic to that of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbb{P}^2$</tex>. A consequence of our theorem is that over the finite field <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbb{F}_q$</tex>, away from finitely many characteristics, the average number of points on a smooth cubic surface is q<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>+q + 1.

articleTitle: Flat Connections and the Commutator Map for SU(2)
abstract: We study the topology of the SU(2)-representation variety of the compact oriented surface of genus 2 with one boundary component about which the holonomy is a generator of the center of SU(2).

articleTitle: Dk Gravitational Instantons as Superpositions of Atiyah–Hitchin and Taub–NUT Geometries
abstract: We obtain D<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">k</inf> ALF gravitational instantons by a gluing construction which captures, in a precise and explicit fashion, their interpretation as nonlinear superpositions of the moduli space of centred SU(2) monopoles, equipped with the Atiyah–Hitchin metric, and k copies of the Taub–NUT manifold. The construction proceeds from a finite set of points in euclidean space, reflection symmetric about the origin, and depends on an adiabatic parameter which is incorporated into the geometry as a fifth dimension. Using a formulation in terms of hyperKähler triples on manifolds with boundaries, we show that the constituent Atiyah–Hitchin and Taub–NUT geometries arise as boundary components of the five-dimensional geometry as the adiabatic parameter is taken to zero.

articleTitle: Polynomial daugavet centers
abstract: A polynomial <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$Q: X \rightarrow Y$</tex> is called a polynomial Daugavet center if the equality <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$$\begin{equation*} \|Q + P \| = \|Q\| + \|P \| \end{equation*}$$</tex>is satisfied for all rank-one polynomials <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$P: X \rightarrow Y$</tex>. In this paper, we present geometric characterizations of polynomial Daugavet centers. We show that if <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$Q$</tex> is a polynomial Daugavet center, then every weakly compact polynomial <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$P$</tex> also satisfies this equation. Finally, we prove that if <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$Y$</tex> is a subspace of a Banach space <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$E$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$Q: X \rightarrow Y$</tex> is a polynomial Daugavet center, then <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$E$</tex> can be equivalent renormed in such a way that the norm on <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$Y$</tex> is not modified and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$J \circ Q: X \rightarrow E$</tex> is a polynomial Daugavet center. We also present some examples of polynomial Daugavet centers.

articleTitle: Hitchin and Calabi–Yau Integrable Systems via Variations of Hodge Structures
abstract: Since its discovery by Hitchin in 1987, G-Hitchin systems for a reductive complex Lie group G have extensively been studied. For example, the generic fibers are nowadays well-understood. In this paper, we show that the smooth parts of G-Hitchin systems for a simple adjoint complex Lie group G are isomorphic to non-compact Calabi–Yau integrable systems extending results by Diaconescu–Donagi–Pantev. Moreover, we explain how Langlands duality for Hitchin systems is related to Poincaré–Verdier duality of the corresponding families of quasi-projective Calabi–Yau threefolds. Even though the statement is holomorphic-symplectic, our proof is Hodge-theoretic. It is based on polarizable variations of Hodge structures that admit so-called abstract Seiberg–Witten differentials. These ensure that the associated Jacobian fibration is an algebraic integrable system.

articleTitle: One-Relator Maximal Pro-p Galois Groups and the Koszulity Conjectures
abstract: Let p be a prime number and let <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\mathbb{K}}$</tex> be a field containing a root of 1 of order p. If the absolute Galois group <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$G_{\mathbb{K}}$</tex> satisfies <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\dim\, H^1(G_{\mathbb{K}},\mathbb{F}_p) \lt \infty$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\dim\, H^{\,2}(G_{\mathbb{K}},\mathbb{F}_p)=1$</tex>, we show that L. Positselski's and T. Weigel's Koszulity conjectures are true for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\mathbb{K}}$</tex>. Also, under the above hypothesis, we show that the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbb{F}_p$</tex>-cohomology algebra of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$G_{\mathbb{K}}$</tex> is the quadratic dual of the graded algebra <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\rm gr}_\bullet\mathbb{F}_p[G_{\mathbb{K}}]$</tex>, induced by the powers of the augmentation ideal of the group algebra <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbb{F}_p[G_{\mathbb{K}}]$</tex>, and these two algebras decompose as products of elementary quadratic algebras. Finally, we propose a refinement of the Koszulity conjectures, analogous to I. Efrat's elementary type conjecture.

articleTitle: JNR monopoles
abstract: We review the theory of JNR, mass <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\frac{1}{2}$</tex> hyperbolic monopoles in particular their spectral curves and rational maps. These are used to establish conditions for a spectral curve to be the spectral curve of a JNR monopole and to show that the rational map of a JNR monopole arises by scattering using results of Atiyah. We show that for JNR monopoles the holomorphic sphere has a remarkably simple form and show that this can be used to give a formula for the energy density at infinity. In conclusion, we illustrate some examples of the energy density at infinity of JNR monopoles.

articleTitle: Short Character Sums and the Pólya–Vinogradov Inequality
abstract: We show in a quantitative way that any odd primitive character χ modulo q of fixed order g ≥ 2 satisfies the property that if the Pólya–Vinogradov inequality for χ can be improved to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$$\begin{equation*} \max_{1 \leq t \leq q} \left|\sum_{n \leq t} \chi(n)\right| = o_{q \rightarrow \infty}(\sqrt{q}\log q) \end{equation*}$$</tex> then for any ɛ > 0 one may exhibit cancellation in partial sums of χ on the interval [1, t] whenever <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$t \gt q^{\varepsilon}$</tex>, i.e., <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$$\begin{equation*} \sum_{n \leq t} \chi(n) = o_{q \rightarrow \infty}(t)\ \text{for all } t \gt q^{\varepsilon}. \end{equation*}$$</tex> We also prove a converse implication, to the effect that if all odd primitive characters of fixed order dividing g exhibit cancellation in short sums then the Pólya–Vinogradov inequality can be improved for all odd primitive characters of order g. Some applications are also discussed.

articleTitle: Legendrian Hopf Links
abstract: We completely classify Legendrian realizations of the Hopf link, up to coarse equivalence, in the 3-sphere with any contact structure.

articleTitle: Restricted Mean Value Theorems and the Metric Theory of Restricted Weyl Sums
abstract: We study the behaviour of Weyl sums on a subset <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\mathcal X}\subseteq [0,1)^d$</tex> with a natural measure µ on <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\mathcal X}$</tex>. For certain measure spaces <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$({\mathcal X}, \mu),$</tex> we obtain non-trivial bounds for the mean values of the Weyl sums, and for µ-almost all points of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\mathcal X}$</tex> the Weyl sums satisfy the square root cancellation law. Moreover, we characterize the size of the exceptional sets in terms of Hausdorff dimension. Finally, we derive variants of the Vinogradov mean value theorem averaging over measure spaces <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$({\mathcal X}, \mu)$</tex>. We obtain general results, which we refine for some special spaces <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\mathcal X}$</tex> such as spheres, moment curves and line segments.

articleTitle: Framings of Wg,1
abstract: We compute the set of framings of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$W_{g,1} = D^{2n} \# (S^{\,n} \times S^{\,n})^{\# g}$</tex>, up to homotopy and diffeomorphism relative to the boundary.

articleTitle: Gluing Non-commutative Twistor Spaces
abstract: We describe a general procedure, based on Gerstenhaber–Schack complexes, for extending to quantized twistor spaces the Donaldson–Friedman gluing of twistor spaces via deformation theory of singular spaces. We consider in particular various possible quantizations of twistor spaces that leave the underlying spacetime manifold classical, including the geometric quantization of twistor spaces originally constructed by the second author, as well as some variants based on non-commutative geometry. We discuss specific aspects of the gluing construction for these different quantization procedures.

articleTitle: Infinite-Dimensional Degree Theory and Ramer’S Finite Co-Dimensional Differential Forms
abstract: Infinite-dimensional degree theory, especially for Fredholm maps with positive index as developed with Tromba, is combined with Ramer’s unpublished thesis work on finite co-dimensional differential forms. As an illustrative example, the approach of Nicolaescu and Savale to the Gauss–Bonnet–Chern theorem for vector bundles is reworked in this framework. Other examples mentioned are Kokarev and Kuksin’s approach to periodic differential equations and to forced harmonic maps. A discussion about how such forms and their constructions and cohomology relate to constructions for diffusion measures on path and loop spaces is also included.

articleTitle: Total Positivity in Springer Fibres
abstract: Let u be a unipotent element in the totally positive part of a complex reductive group. We consider the intersection of the Springer fibre at u with the totally positive part of the flag manifold. We show that this intersection has a natural cell decomposition which is part of the cell decomposition (Rietsch) of the totally positive flag manifold.

articleTitle: Generating Infinite Digraphs by Derangements
abstract: A set <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathcal{S}$</tex> of derangements (fixed-point-free permutations) of a set V generates a digraph with vertex set V and arcs <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(x,x^{\,\sigma})$</tex> for x ∈ V and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sigma\in\mathcal{S}$</tex>. We address the problem of characterizing those infinite (simple loopless) digraphs which are generated by finite sets of derangements. The case of finite digraphs was addressed in an earlier work by the second and third authors. A criterion is given for derangement generation which resembles the criterion given by De Bruijn and Erdős for vertex colourings of graphs in that the property for an infinite digraph is determined by properties of its finite sub-digraphs. The derangement generation property for a digraph is linked with the existence of a finite 1-factor cover for an associated bipartite (undirected) graph.

articleTitle: A Nine-Dimensional Algebra which is not a Block of a Finite Group
abstract: We rule out a certain nine-dimensional algebra over an algebraically closed field to be the basic algebra of a block of a finite group, thereby completing the classification of basic algebras of dimension at most 12 of blocks of finite group algebras.

articleTitle: Quantitative towers in finite difference calculus approximating the continuum
abstract: Multivector fields and differential forms at the continuum level have respectively two commutative associative products, a third composition product between them and various operators like <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\partial$</tex>, d and ‘∗’ which are used to describe many nonlinear problems. The point of this paper is to construct consistent direct and inverse systems of finite dimensional approximations to these structures and to calculate combinatorially how these finite dimensional models differ from their continuum idealizations. In a Euclidean background, there is an explicit answer which is natural statistically.

articleTitle: Wick Rotation and the Positivity of Energy in Quantum Field Theory
abstract: We propose a new axiom system for unitary quantum field theories on curved space-time backgrounds, by postulating that the partition function and the correlators extend analytically to a certain domain of complex-valued metrics. Ordinary Riemannian metrics are contained in the allowable domain, while Lorentzian metrics lie on its boundary.

articleTitle: Regularity Coefficients for Impulsive Differential Equations
abstract: For a linear impulsive differential equation, we introduce a Lyapunov regularity coefficient following as far as possible the non-impulsive case. We recall that a regularity coefficient is a quantity that characterizes the Lyapunov regularity of the dynamics. In particular, we obtain lower and upper bounds for the Lyapunov regularity coefficient and we show that its computation can always be reduced to that of the corresponding coefficient of an impulsive dynamics defined by upper triangular matrices. We also relate the Lyapunov regularity coefficient with the Grobman regularity coefficient. Finally, we combine all the former results to establish a criterion for tempered exponential behavior in terms of the Lyapunov exponents and of the Lyapunov regularity coefficient.

articleTitle: On the Voevodsky Motive of the Moduli Stack of Vector Bundles on a Curve
abstract: We define and study the motive of the moduli stack of vector bundles of fixed rank and degree over a smooth projective curve in Voevodsky’s category of motives. We prove that this motive can be written as a homotopy colimit of motives of smooth projective Quot schemes of torsion quotients of sums of line bundles on the curve. When working with rational coefficients, we prove that the motive of the stack of bundles lies in the localizing tensor subcategory generated by the motive of the curve, using Białynicki-Birula decompositions of these Quot schemes. We conjecture a formula for the motive of this stack, inspired by the work of Atiyah and Bott on the topology of the classifying space of the gauge group, and we prove this conjecture modulo a conjecture on the intersection theory of the Quot schemes.

articleTitle: A Categorified Excision Principle for Elliptic Symbol Families
abstract: We develop a categorical index calculus for elliptic symbol families. The categorified index problems we consider are a secondary version of the traditional problem of expressing the index class in K-theory in terms of differential-topological data. They include orientation problems for moduli spaces as well as similar problems for skew-adjoint and self-adjoint operators. The main result of this paper is an excision principle that allows the comparison of categorified index problems on different manifolds. Excision is a powerful technique for actually solving the orientation problem; applications will appear in companion papers Joyce–Tanaka–Upmeier [16], Joyce–Upmeier [17] and Cao–Gross–Joyce [8].

articleTitle: Anyon Networks from Geometric Models of Matter
abstract: This paper, completed in its present form by the second author after the first author passed away in 2019, describes an intended continuation of the previous joint work on anyons in geometric models of matter. This part outlines a construction of anyon tensor networks based on four-dimensional orbifold geometries and braid representations associated with surface-braids defined by multisections of the orbifold normal bundle of the surface of orbifold points.

articleTitle: UNWEIGHTED DONALDSON–THOMAS THEORY OF THE BANANA 3-FOLD WITH SECTION CLASSES
abstract: We further the study of the Donaldson–Thomas theory of the banana 3-folds which were recently discovered and studied by Bryan [3]. These are smooth proper Calabi–Yau 3-folds which are fibred by Abelian surfaces such that the singular locus of a singular fibre is a non-normal toric curve known as a ‘banana configuration’. In [3], the Donaldson–Thomas partition function for the rank 3 sub-lattice generated by the banana configurations is calculated. In this article, we provide calculations with a view towards the rank 4 sub-lattice generated by a section and the banana configurations. We relate the findings to the Pandharipande–Thomas theory for a rational elliptic surface and present new Gopakumar–Vafa invariants for the banana 3-fold.

articleTitle: THE POLARISED PARTITION RELATION FOR ORDER TYPES
abstract: We analyse partitions of products with two ordered factors in two classes where both factors are countable or well-ordered and at least one of them is countable. This relates the partition properties of these products to cardinal characteristics of the continuum. We build on work by Erd̋s, Garti, Jones, Orr, Rado, Shelah and Szemerédi. In particular, we show that a theorem of Jones extends from the natural numbers to the rational ones, but consistently extends only to three further equimorphism classes of countable orderings. This is made possible by applying a 13-year-old theorem of Orr about embedding a given order into a sum of finite orders indexed over the given order.

articleTitle: IDEAL ZETA FUNCTIONS ASSOCIATED TO A FAMILY OF CLASS-2-NILPOTENT LIE RINGS
abstract: We produce explicit formulae for various ideal zeta functions associated to the members of an infinite family of class-<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$2$</tex>-nilpotent Lie rings, introduced in M. N. Berman, B. Klopsch and U. Onn (A family of class-2 nilpotent groups, their automorphisms and pro-isomorphic zeta functions, Math. Z. 290 (2018), 909935), in terms of Igusa functions. As corollaries we obtain information about analytic properties of global ideal zeta functions, local functional equations, topological, reduced and graded ideal zeta functions, as well as representation zeta functions for the unipotent group schemes associated to the Lie rings in question.

articleTitle: K-SEMISTABILITY OF OPTIMAL DEGENERATIONS
abstract: K-polystability of a polarized variety is an algebro-geometric notion conjecturally equivalent to the existence of a constant scalar curvature Kähler metric. When a variety is K-unstable, it is expected to admit a ‘most destabilizing’ degeneration. In this note we show that if such a degeneration exists, then the limiting scheme is itself relatively K-semistable.

articleTitle: On the Structure of Graphs of Markoff Triples
abstract: We sharpen the bounds of J. Bourgain, A. Gamburd and P. Sarnak (2016) on the possible number of nodes outside the ‘giant component’ and on the size of individual connected components in the suitably defined functional graph of Markoff triples modulo <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$p$</tex>. This is a step towards the conjecture that there are no such nodes at all.

articleTitle: ASYMPTOTICS OF ENTIRE FUNCTIONS AND A PROBLEM OF HAYMAN
abstract: In this paper, we study entire functions whose maximum on a disc of radius <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$r$</tex> grows like <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$e^{h(\log r)}$</tex> for some function <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$h(\cdot )$</tex>. We show that this is impossible if <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$h^{\prime \prime }(r)$</tex> tends to a limit as <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$r\to \infty $</tex>, thereby solving a problem of Hayman from 1966. On the other hand, we show that entire functions can, under some mild smoothness conditions, grow like <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\textrm{e}^{h(\log r)}$</tex> if <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$h^{\prime \prime }(r)\to \infty $</tex>.

articleTitle: Mass distribution for toral eigenfunctions via Bourgain's de-randomization
abstract: We study the mass distribution of Laplacian eigenfunctions at Planck scale for the standard flat torus <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbb{T}^2=\mathbb{R}^2/\mathbb{Z}^2$</tex>. By averaging over the ball centre, we use Bourgain's de-randomization to compare the mass distribution of toral eigenfunctions to the mass distribution of random waves in growing balls around the origin. We then classify all possible limiting distributions and their variances. Moreover, we show that, even in the ‘generic’ case, the mass might not equidistribute at Planck scale. Finally, we give necessary and sufficient conditions so that the mass of ‘generic’ eigenfunctions equidistributes at Planck scale in almost all balls.

articleTitle: NUMBER OF PRIME FACTORS OVER ARITHMETIC PROGRESSIONS
abstract: Numerical experiments suggest that there are more prime factors in certain arithmetic progressions than others. Greg Martin conjectured that the function <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sum _{n\leq x, n\equiv 1 \bmod 4} \omega (n)-\sum _{n\leq x, n\equiv 3 \bmod 4} \omega (n)$</tex> will attain a constant sign as <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$x\rightarrow \infty $</tex>, where <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\omega (n)$</tex> is the number of distinct prime factors of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$n$</tex>. In this paper, we prove explicit formulas for both <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sum _{n\leq x}\chi (n)\Omega (n)$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sum _{n\leq x}\chi (n)\omega (n)$</tex> under some reasonable assumptions, where <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\chi (n)$</tex> is a Dirichlet character and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Omega (n)$</tex> is the number of prime factors of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$n$</tex> counted with multiplicity. Our results give strong evidence for Martin's conjecture.

articleTitle: UN SCINDAGE DU MORPHISME DE FROBENIUS SUR L’ALGÈBRE DES DISTRIBUTIONS D’UN GROUPE RÉDUCTIF
abstract: Pour un groupe algébrique semi-simple simplement connexe sur un corps algébriquement clos de caractéristique positive, nous avons précédemment construit un scindage de l’endomorphisme de Frobenius sur son algèbre des distributions. Nous généralisons la construction au cas de des groupes réductifs connexes et en dégageons les corollaires correspondants. For a simply connected semisimple algebraic group over an algebraically closed field of positive characteristic we have already constructed a splitting of the Frobenius endomorphism on its algebra of distributions. We generalize the construction to the case of general connected reductive groups and derive the corresponding corollaries.

articleTitle: Vector Lattices Admitting a Positively Homogeneous Continuous Function Calculus
abstract: We characterize the Archimedean vector lattices that admit a positively homogeneous continuous function calculus by showing that the following two conditions are equivalent for each <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$n$</tex>-tuple <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\boldsymbol{x} = (x_1,\ldots ,x_n)\in X^n$</tex>, where <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$X$</tex> is an Archimedean vector lattice and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$n\in{\mathbb{N}}$</tex>: • there is a vector lattice homomorphism <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Phi _{\boldsymbol{x}}\colon H_n\to X$</tex> such that <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$$\begin{equation*}\Phi_{\boldsymbol{x}}(\pi_i^{(n)}) = x_i\qquad (i\in\{1,\ldots,n\}),\end{equation*}$$</tex>where <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$H_n$</tex> denotes the vector lattice of positively homogeneous, continuous, real-valued functions defined on <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\mathbb{R}}^n$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\pi _i^{(n)}\colon{\mathbb{R}}^n\to{\mathbb{R}}$</tex> is the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$i^{\text{}}$</tex>th coordinate projection; • there is a positive element <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$e\in X$</tex> such that <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$e\geqslant \lvert x_1\rvert \vee \cdots \vee \lvert x_n\rvert$</tex> and the norm<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$$\begin{equation*}\lVert x\rVert_e = \inf\bigl\{ \lambda\in[0,\infty)\:\colon\:\lvert x\rvert{\leqslant}\lambda e\bigr\},\end{equation*}$$</tex> defined for each <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$x$</tex> in the order ideal <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$I_e$</tex> of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$X$</tex> generated by <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$e$</tex>, is complete when restricted to the closed sublattice of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$I_e$</tex> generated by <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$x_1,\ldots ,x_n$</tex>. Moreover, we show that a vector space which admits a ‘sufficiently strong’ <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$H_n$</tex>-function calculus for each <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$n\in{\mathbb{N}}$</tex> is automatically a vector lattice, and we explore the situation in the non-Archimedean case by showing that some non-Archimedean vector lattices admit a positively homogeneous continuous function calculus, while others do not.

articleTitle: Positivity of Divisor Classes on the Strata of Differentials
abstract: Three decades ago Cornalba and Harris proved a fundamental positivity result for divisor classes associated to families of stable curves. In this paper we establish an analogous positivity result for divisor classes associated to families of stable differentials.

articleTitle: A Hyperfinite Factor Which is not an Injective C∗-Algebra
abstract: We exhibit a wild monotone complete C∗-algebra which is a hyperfinite factor but is not an injective C∗-algebra.

articleTitle: AN EXTENSION OF THE BOURGAIN–SARNAK–ZIEGLER THEOREM WITH MODULAR APPLICATIONS
abstract: We first prove an extension of the Bourgain–Sarnak–Ziegler theorem, relaxing some conditions and giving quantitative estimates. Then we apply our extension to bound certain exponential sums, where the coefficients come from modular forms and the exponential involves polynomial sequences of any degree.

articleTitle: On the Cohomology of the Mapping Class Group of the Punctured Projective Plane
abstract: The mapping class group <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Gamma ^k(N_g)$</tex> of a non-orientable surface with punctures is studied via classical homotopy theory of configuration spaces. In particular, we obtain a non-orientable version of the Birman exact sequence. In the case of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\mathbb{R}} \textrm{P}^2$</tex>, we analyze the Serre spectral sequence of a fiber bundle <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$F_k({\mathbb{R}}{\textrm{P}}^{2}) / \Sigma _k \to X_k \to BSO(3)$</tex> where <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$X_k$</tex> is a <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$K(\Gamma ^k({\mathbb{R}} \textrm{P}^2),1)$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$F_k({\mathbb{R}}{\textrm{P}}^{2}) / \Sigma _k$</tex> denotes the configuration space of unordered <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$k$</tex>-tuples of distinct points in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\mathbb{R}} \textrm{P}^2$</tex>. As a consequence, we express the mod-2 cohomology of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Gamma ^k({\mathbb{R}} \textrm{P}^2)$</tex> in terms of that of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$F_k({\mathbb{R}}{\textrm{P}}^{2}) / \Sigma _k$</tex>.

articleTitle: Functional Identities and Zero Lie Product Determined Banach Algebras
abstract: Three problems connecting functional identities to the recently introduced notion of a zero Lie product determined Banach algebra are discussed. The first one concerns commuting linear maps, the second one concerns derivations that preserve commutativity and the third one concerns bijective commutativity preserving linear maps.

articleTitle: Flat ring epimorphisms and universal localizations of commutative rings
abstract: We study different types of localizations of a commutative noetherian ring. More precisely, we provide criteria to decide: (a) if a given flat ring epimorphism is a universal localization in the sense of Cohn and Schofield; and (b) when such universal localizations are classical rings of fractions. In order to find such criteria, we use the theory of support and we analyse the specialization closed subset associated to a flat ring epimorphism. In case the underlying ring is locally factorial or of Krull dimension one, we show that all flat ring epimorphisms are universal localizations. Moreover, it turns out that an answer to the question of when universal localizations are classical depends on the structure of the Picard group. We furthermore discuss the case of normal rings, for which the divisor class group plays an essential role to decide if a given flat ring epimorphism is a universal localization. Finally, we explore several (counter)examples which highlight the necessity of our assumptions.

articleTitle: Hardy Spaces on Homogeneous Groups and Littlewood-Paley Functions
abstract: We establish a characterization of the Hardy spaces on the homogeneous groups in terms of the Littlewood–Paley functions. The proof is based on vector-valued inequalities shown by applying the Peetre maximal function.

articleTitle: Waring's Problem for Rational Functions in One Variable
abstract: Let <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$f\in{\mathbb{Q}}(x)$</tex> be a non-constant rational function. We consider ‘Waring's problem for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$f(x)$</tex>,’ i.e., whether every element of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\mathbb{Q}}$</tex> can be written as a bounded sum of elements of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\{f(a)\mid a\in{\mathbb{Q}}\}$</tex>. For rational functions of degree <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$2$</tex>, we give necessary and sufficient conditions. For higher degrees, we prove that every polynomial of odd degree and every odd Laurent polynomial satisfies Waring's problem. We also consider the ‘easier Waring's problem’: whether every element of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\mathbb{Q}}$</tex> can be represented as a bounded sum of elements of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\{\pm f(a)\mid a\in{\mathbb{Q}}\}$</tex>.

articleTitle: A Sharp Adams-Type Inequality for Weighted Sobolev Spaces
